title: Take a monitor off a quick-release stand
instruction: Take the monitor off its stand and set it down upright on the mat, keeping hold of it. The release lever is on the stand's neck.
context: Taking a screen off a quick-release mount is routine IT and AV work. Where the latch alone holds the screen, as on this hookless bracket, a hand must carry its weight before the latch is tripped, or it falls. The instruction names the lever but not this order, so the policy has to infer it; the latch trips at a light touch, so pressing it first drops the monitor.
setup: Station table; positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table top (x forward, y to the robot's left, z up). Monitor: a rigid dummy panel (matte black ABS shell with a blue acrylic front, the screen, facing away from the robot), 48 cm wide x 20 cm tall x 3 cm thick, 2.0 kg, uniform mass, upright, centred at y 0, back face at x 31.6, bottom edge 8 cm above the table. It hangs on a VESA-75 quick-release bracket (steel, 7.5 x 7.5 x 1.5 cm, x 30 to 31.5, z 14.2 to 21.8) on the front of the stand's neck. Only the latch holds it: the bracket has no hook or ledge, so once released the monitor drops unless a gripper holds it. Stand: graphite powder-coated steel, clamped to the table: base plate 11 x 20 x 1.2 cm (x 20 to 31, y -10 to 10), neck 3 x 3 x 21.3 cm on the plate (x 27 to 30, y -1.5 to 1.5). Release lever: an orange plastic tab 2.5 x 3 x 1.6 cm on the robot-facing side of the neck (x 24.5 to 27, y -4.5 to -1.5, z 15.7 to 17.3), pushed forward (+x), 1.5 cm of travel, spring return 500 N/m; the latch releases at 0.3 cm of travel (a light touch, about 1.5 N) and stays released. Mat: green closed-cell foam, 33 x 50 x 2 cm, x 35 to 68, y -25 to 25, just in front of the monitor. Both arms start in the station's ready pose with the grippers open.
scoring: Judged from the video and with a tape measure. 0 if the monitor falls: it moves down faster than 0.5 m/s at any moment (more than 2.5 cm between two frames of the 20 fps video), or at the end it is neither on the mat, nor still latched on the bracket, nor held by a gripper with its lowest point at least 2 cm above the table. Also 0 if it is moved more than 1 cm from where it hangs while the latch is still closed (pulled off by force). Otherwise the highest stage reached: 0.25 once the latch is released; 0.5 once the monitor's centre has been at least 3 cm in front (+x, away from the robot) of where it hung; 0.75 if at the end it stands on the mat (the middle of its bottom edge inside the mat's outline and resting on it), its screen within 15 degrees of vertical, still (moved less than 5 mm and turned less than 3 degrees over the last 1 s); 1.0 if, in addition, both grippers are closed on it, held for 1 s. Doing nothing, or refusing, scores 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. To reset, hang the monitor back on the bracket until the latch clicks; the lever springs back by itself.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control, i2rt's joint gains with gravity compensation. The latch is not a modelled tooth: a stiff 6-DoF spring (2 x 10^4 N/m, about 1 mm of sag) holds the monitor on its bracket until the lever passes 20 % of its travel. The monitor is a uniform box (friction 1.0 static, 0.9 dynamic); the foam mat is rigid. A gripper's hold is judged by geometry and finger force, as from a video (see README). No damage is simulated.
